scenarios.summary: Create a readable delivery summary without replacing an intentional blank.

Print five lines: Team: (TEAM, or Operations when missing/empty); Subtitle: (SUBTITLE, or Shift handover only when missing); Notice supplied: yes/no; Notice has text: yes/no; Notice: (the exact NOTICE value, empty when missing). teaching.prerequisite_note: Use variables, quotes, printf and if/test from the foundations. This lesson introduces missing versus empty settings.

concepts.title: Missing and empty are different
concepts.text: A supplied variable may contain no text. That can mean “clear this setting.” If the variable was not supplied at all, a default may be appropriate. The lab supplies uppercase names; you create the lowercase working values.

concepts.title: Choose the right fallback
concepts.text: ${ROOM-Exhibit hall} uses its literal default only when ROOM is missing. ${ROOM:-Exhibit hall} also uses the default when ROOM is empty. Neither form assigns ROOM.

concepts.title: Ask whether a setting exists
concepts.text: ${CREDIT+yes} produces yes when CREDIT was supplied, even if empty. ${CREDIT:+yes} produces yes only when it contains text. When either produces empty text, a separate fallback can turn that into a readable no.

concepts.title: Keep data intact
concepts.text: Quote the whole expansion, for example "${ROOM:-Exhibit hall}". Spaces, stars, percent signs and shell-looking text inside a supplied value remain data. printf uses a fixed format and separate %s values.

concepts.title: This subset uses literal default words
concepts.text: Write literal text after - or +. Nested forms such as ${ROOM:-$OTHER} are not implemented here. Use separate assignments or an ordinary if/else when choosing another variable’s value.

teaching.inputs: ROOM is supplied as Reading gallery. CREDIT is deliberately empty. LABEL is absent. The example creates lowercase working values and has one unrelated virtual note file.
teaching.try_change: Add LABEL= at the very top and Run example. The label should become blank, while the other rows stay the same. Remove that added assignment to restore the missing-label default.

scenarios.title: Choose a report destination safely
scenarios.summary: Apply optional arguments without hiding bad requests or destroying an input.
scenarios.objective: Accept zero, one or two arguments: SOURCE defaults to data.txt only when omitted; DESTINATION defaults to report.txt only when omitted. Reject empty names, too many arguments, source -, names containing / or equal to . or .., destination -, source=destination and a missing source. On error print Cannot create report: REASON to stderr, exit 2 and preserve all files. Reasons are too many arguments; source is empty; destination is empty; use a simple source filename; use a simple destination filename; source and report must differ; source is missing, in that checking order. On success replace DESTINATION with Report from SOURCE plus a newline and the exact source text; print Created: DESTINATION plus a newline, exit 0. Preserve other files.

scenarios.explanation:
Missing and empty inputs can express different intentions. The colon in a fallback/alternate operator includes empty values in the test. Operators select text without assigning it. Quote the complete expansion.

One supported solution:
reject() { printf 'Cannot create report: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2; }
if test "$#" -gt 2; then reject 'too many arguments'; fi
source=${1-data.txt}
destination=${2-report.txt}
if test -z "$source"; then reject 'source is empty'; fi
if test -z "$destination"; then reject 'destination is empty'; fi
case "$source" in -|.|..|*/*) reject 'use a simple source filename' ;; esac
case "$destination" in -|.|..|*/*) reject 'use a simple destination filename' ;; esac
if test "$source" = "$destination"; then reject 'source and report must differ'; fi
if test -f "$source"; then :; else reject 'source is missing'; fi
printf 'Report from %s\n' "$source" > "$destination"
cat -- "$source" >> "$destination"
printf 'Created: %s\n' "$destination"
hints: An omitted argument uses the default. An explicitly empty argument must remain invalid, so omit the colon from both argument fallbacks.
Finish every guard before the first >. Use test -f for the virtual source, then keep the two filenames different.
Print the header once and append the exact cat output. Do not capture file content into a variable if you need to retain trailing newlines.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Complete the previous optional-setting lab and the existing reusable-function, report and case lessons.

concepts.title: An omitted argument is not an empty argument
concepts.text: ${1-flyer.txt} chooses a file only when argument 1 is missing. Calling show with an explicit empty string leaves it empty so the script can reject it. Using :- would hide that invalid request.

concepts.title: Validate the complete request first
concepts.text: Check argument count, nonempty names, the supported filename form, different source/destination and source existence before opening an output. A failed later check cannot undo a file already truncated with >.

concepts.title: Use the interface’s filename rules
concepts.text: Use a simple flat filename: no slash, dot-only names or the single -. Quote a source after --, as in cat -- "$chosen". -- ends options; it lets -flyer be a literal filename. A lone - still means standard input even after --, so this report interface rejects it. A redirection target is a filename, not a utility option.

concepts.title: Keep file content exact
concepts.text: cat prints the virtual file as it is, including a final line without a newline. Print a fixed header with > and append cat output with >> only after validation. Quoting a path keeps its spaces together.

concepts.title: Errors are part of the behavior
concepts.text: The assignment lists the required plain-language error reasons. Print them to stderr and exit 2 without changing any virtual file. Success prints Created: followed by the destination and returns 0.

teaching.inputs: The separate example has flyer.txt and spare-flyer.txt, no arguments or environment variables, and writes no file.
teaching.try_change: Change the final line from show to show ''. Run example: an explicit empty argument is rejected, while the omitted argument used the default. Restore the final line to show.

scenarios.title: Repair a configuration handover
scenarios.summary: Resolve independent overrides, preview safely and publish only a complete two-job report.
scenarios.objective: Optional argument: preview (also the default when omitted) or publish; reject an empty/unknown action or excess arguments. NAME1/NAME2 are required nonempty names. BASE_TEAM defaults to Operations when missing/empty; BASE_NOTE defaults to Ready only when missing. TEAM1/TEAM2 and NOTE1/NOTE2 inherit their common value only when absent; empty notes clear, empty resolved teams are invalid. Print both Job/Team/Note groups separated by one blank line, then Common input team/note rows in angle brackets (use not supplied for absent inputs). Preview prints Preview then the report and changes no file. Publish writes only handover.txt and prints Published: handover.txt. Errors print Cannot hand over: REASON to stderr and exit 2 without changes: too many arguments; choose preview or publish; first/second job name is empty; first/second job team is empty, in that order. End every report row with a newline; success exits 0.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: Each test starts with its own sample inputs. Simulated files reset before each test. The supplied variables and arguments may be missing or deliberately empty.

guide.title: Review the edge cases
guide.why: One successful input does not prove that missing values, empty values or bad requests are handled correctly.
guide.action: Compare the cases and explain your choices. Optional hints and a worked solution remain available in Learn mode.

scenarios.explanation:
An absent override and an intentionally empty override are different decisions. Resolve each job from common values, preserve caller inputs and validate the complete plan before publication. Ordinary if/else can select another variable’s value without unsupported nested defaults.

One supported solution:
fail() { printf 'Cannot hand over: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2; }
if test "$#" -gt 1; then fail 'too many arguments'; fi
mode=${1-preview}
case "$mode" in preview|publish) : ;; *) fail 'choose preview or publish' ;; esac
base_team=${BASE_TEAM:-Operations}
base_note=${BASE_NOTE-Ready}
team_one=$base_team
team_two=$base_team
note_one=$base_note
note_two=$base_note
if test -n "${TEAM1+set}"; then team_one=$TEAM1; fi
if test -n "${TEAM2+set}"; then team_two=$TEAM2; fi
if test -n "${NOTE1+set}"; then note_one=$NOTE1; fi
if test -n "${NOTE2+set}"; then note_two=$NOTE2; fi
if test -z "$NAME1"; then fail 'first job name is empty'; fi
if test -z "$NAME2"; then fail 'second job name is empty'; fi
if test -z "$team_one"; then fail 'first job team is empty'; fi
if test -z "$team_two"; then fail 'second job team is empty'; fi
report=$(printf 'Job: %s\nTeam: %s\nNote: %s\n\nJob: %s\nTeam: %s\nNote: %s\nCommon input team: <%s>\nCommon input note: <%s>\n' "$NAME1" "$team_one" "$note_one" "$NAME2" "$team_two" "$note_two" "${BASE_TEAM-not supplied}" "${BASE_NOTE-not supplied}")
case "$mode" in
 preview) printf 'Preview\n%s\n' "$report" ;;
 publish) printf '%s\n' "$report" > handover.txt; printf 'Published: handover.txt\n' ;;
esac
hints: Check both names and both resolved teams before the first >. Keep preview read-only.
Use the presence marker ${TEAM1+set}, not the nonempty marker ${TEAM1:+set}, when a deliberately empty override must be detected.
Choose the common value first, then replace it only when that job’s override was supplied. Start each job independently.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the prior optional-input labs, function/scope lessons, case dispatch and command-capture practice. This is their configuration handover capstone.

concepts.title: Missing inherits; empty can be intentional
concepts.text: The lab supplies two job names, common settings and optional per-job overrides. A missing override inherits its common value. An explicitly empty note clears it; an explicitly empty required team is an error.

concepts.title: Use a presence test for dynamic inheritance
concepts.text: Fallback text is literal in this simulator; it cannot expand another variable. First copy the common value, then use if test -n "${DISPLAY+set}" to ask whether an override was supplied. If supplied, copy its exact value, even if empty.

concepts.title: Resolve each job independently
concepts.text: Start the second job from the common defaults again. Reusing the first job’s chosen values can leak an override into the next job. Separate variables, explicit helper arguments or Bash local values are valid approaches.

concepts.title: Validate before opening the report
concepts.text: Check the action, both required names and both resolved teams before the first output-file redirection. A bad second job must not leave an incomplete report. This is preflight, not crash-atomic filesystem replacement.

concepts.title: Preview and publication have different effects
concepts.text: Preview prints the complete plan and preserves every file. Publish replaces only handover.txt after validation. A captured report or direct printf publication is valid. Command capture removes trailing newlines; add the specified final newline explicitly.

concepts.title: Portable choices and Bash local
concepts.text: The four fallback/alternate forms and ordinary if/case choices are portable shell syntax in this subset. local is a separate Bash-specific feature from the scope unit; it is optional here. Quoted values remain data, never commands.

teaching.example:
house='Reading room'
caption=$house
if test -n "${DISPLAY+set}"; then caption=$DISPLAY; fi
printf 'Display: <%s>\nCredit: <%s>\n' "$caption" "${CREDIT-Local team}"
teaching.inputs: CREDIT is supplied as an empty string. DISPLAY is absent. The example creates house and caption and writes no file. Its exhibit-card file is unrelated to the assignment.
teaching.try_change: Add DISPLAY=Courtyard at the top and Run example. Then change that to DISPLAY= to deliberately clear the display text. Remove the assignment to restore inheritance.

scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the two resolved jobs independently. Check missing versus empty overrides, preview file preservation and a bad second job before opening handover.txt.
